Hi Olga / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A few follow-ups from our finance and SRE teams:

- We need a clear breakdown of retention costs by tier (30d/90d/365d) for traces and dashboard storage, including per-GB egress assumptions.
- On dashboards: can you confirm whether the advanced dashboard SKU includes live query concurrency or if that carries an extra surface fee? Our platform runs a mix of scheduled and ad-hoc live dashboards.

Can you send a simple scenario (month-by-month cost) and a sample SOW line items so our procurement can review?

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Exploring observability add-on pricing (retention + dashboards)

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. Key asks: tiered retention costs, surface fee for live concurrency, and proration rules.

I started a draft response and a quick scenario in the attached pricing PDF. Notes:
- Our standard advanced dashboard SKU covers up to 5 live-concurrent queries per org; additional concurrency is billed as a surface add-on (per-concurrency block).
- Retention is priced by effective ingested storage and a daily storage multiplier; we can offer a 10% discount at >50TB committed annual retention.
- Proration: we prorate the delta on storage only (not one-time onboarding fees) and apply the new tier from the next billing cycle; for mid-cycle changes we credit unused days on the old tier.

Requests from me:
1) Ben — can you validate the concurrency block pricing below? I proposed $1,200 per additional concurrency block / month.
2) Jordan — packaging: can we surface an intermediate 180d tier (30/180/365) to reduce a big jump?
3) Kim — legal will want explicit SOW language for proration; can you draft a short clause we can propose to Acme Legal?

I attached: redwood-observability-pricing-v3.pdf (draft scenarios)

Thanks — OL

--
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Exploring observability add-on pricing (retention + dashboards)

OL — quick notes on numbers after reviewing Acme's export: 

- Concurrency: $1,200 / block / month is a fine starting point for negotiation. Suggest offering first block at $800 for the first 6 months as an intro concession.
- Retention tiers: agree on a 180d middle tier; pricing suggestion (per TB/month equivalent): 30d=$12/TB/mo, 180d=$5.5/TB/mo, 365d=$3.8/TB/mo. These reflect storage + indexing overhead + trace index rebuild costs.
- Volume discount: for commits >= 60TB/month we can move to a 12% committed discount vs list.
- Proration mechanics: we should make the credit calculation explicit: credit = unused days * current tier rate; new charge = remaining days * new tier rate. Mention rounding and minimum $50 adjustment floor to avoid tiny transactions.

I'll prepare a clean SOW snippet for Kim to slot into the proposal.

Ben
VP, Product & GTM
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Exploring observability add-on pricing (retention + dashboards)

Adding packaging input — my recommendation to make this easier to consume for procurement:

- Offer three named bundles: Essentials (30d traces, basic dashboards), Growth (180d traces, advanced dashboards incl. 5 concurrent queries), and Enterprise (365d + unlimited concurrency surface option).
- For Growth bundle, include a one-time migration credit ($5k) if customer commits to 12 months at >= 40TB/mo. This helps them test longer retention without upfront cost spikes.
- Surface fee model: rather than per-concurrency block only, also allow per-seat dashboard viewers for smaller teams — simpler for customers who have many viewers but low concurrency.

If we present as bundles with clear upgrade paths and an explicit proration clause, procurement tends to sign faster. I can mock a short slide with the three bundles if helpful.

Jordan
Director, Solutions

To: Carlos Mendez <carlos@acmedata.com>, contracts@acmedata.com

Subject: Updated proposal: retention tiers, bundles, and proration clause (draft)

Hi Carlos / Acme team —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short draft that (1) lays out monthly cost scenarios using the usage extract you sent, (2) describes three bundles and optional surface fees, and (3) includes the proration clause language for legal review. Highlights: 

- Proposed bundles (monthly list price): Essentials = $9/TB (30d traces + basic dashboards); Growth = $5.5/TB (180d + advanced dashboards incl. 5 concurrent queries); Enterprise = $3.8/TB (365d) + optional concurrency blocks at $1,200/block/mo.
- Intro concession: first concurrency block at $800 for months 1–6 if you commit to 12 months.
- Commit discount: 12% off list for commits >= 60TB/mo.
- Proration (draft SOW clause): "When a Customer requests a retention tier change mid-billing cycle, Redwood will credit the Customer for the unused portion of the existing retention tier at the then-applicable rate and invoice the Customer for the remainder of the billing cycle at the new retention tier rate. Credits and charges below $50 per invoice period will be netted and not invoiced separately."

Attachments: redwood-observability-pricing-v3.pdf (scenario pages), acme-retention-model-v1.xlsx (reference)

Next steps:
1) Carlos — can you confirm which bundle maps to your org (Essentials/Growth/Enterprise) and whether you want us to include the migration credit for Growth?
2) Contracts@acmedata.com — please flag any SOW language edits.
3) I'll propose a short call next Tue to walk through numbers if helpful.

Thanks and open to tradeoffs —
Olga
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
